hints.content:
$g$ is increasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $g(x)$ also increases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going upwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by four. The graph of y equals g of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative four, fourteen and the x-intercept negative two, zero. It continues to decrease through the y-intercept zero, negative five and one-half until the local minimum at one-half, negative six. Then it increases through the point two, negative four, the x-intercept three, zero and the point four, six. All values are estimated. The function is highlighted after x equals one-half.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $g$ increasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-5<x<-2$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g$ is decreasing on this interval
$-2<x<0$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g$ is decreasing on this interval
$2<x<5$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
